title: The 7 Money Levels: Where Are You in 2027?
description:
There are seven money levels, from drowning in debt to truly free, and most people are stuck on level two. In this video I walk through all seven levels with the real numbers, how to tell which one you're on, and exactly what moves you up to the next one.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:18 How we got the numbers
2:02 The big picture
3:00 Level 1. Underwater
4:24 Level 2. Paycheck to paycheck
5:51 Level 3. The starter cushion
7:25 Level 4. Stable
8:51 Level 5. Momentum
10:13 Level 6. Millionaire
11:36 Level 7. Financially independent
13:00 Angle 1: The numbers behind each level
16:16 Angle 2: The psychology of each level
19:56 Angle 3: The playbook for each level
22:40 How long each level takes
23:54 Three example climbs
26:56 Five mistakes that drop you a level
28:07 Questions people ask
30:06 Recap: the 7 levels
31:17 What to do next

Sources:
- Federal Reserve, Survey of Consumer Finances 2022 (median net worth $192,700, mean $1,063,700; by age: under 35 $39,040, 35-44 $135,300, 45-54 $246,700)
- Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025 (63% would cover a $400 expense with cash; about 1 in 5 experienced fraud or scams)
- Bankrate, Emergency Savings Report (about 1 in 4 Americans have no emergency savings)
- Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Quarterly Report on Household Debt and Credit (total household debt above $18 trillion)
- Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit (credit card interest rates above 20%)
- UBS Global Wealth Report 2025 (more than 20 million millionaires in the United States)
- William P. Bengen, Determining Withdrawal Rates Using Historical Data, Journal of Financial Planning (1994)
- Compound growth: stated illustrative math at 7% average yearly return, compounded monthly

Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors. Full credits and licenses: https://github.com/ryan-rover-money-channel/ryan-rover-money/blob/main/agendamento/creditos/video03.md

This video is for education only and is not financial advice. Numbers are illustrations, not promises.
